subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Gateway multi-token principal model for Control UI and webchat token-mode users, and should that model be unified with the scoped-token work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367?
rationale: The request changes public auth config, credential matching, caller identity, session isolation, and authorization semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security/product boundary.

options.title: Design Unified Principals
options.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal contract that covers per-user tokens, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation/revocation, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To User Labels
options.body: Implement only token-to-user labels and session identity for Control UI/webchat now, accepting possible later migration into a broader scoped-token model.

options.title: Keep External Front Layers
options.body: Decline native multi-token auth for now and document trusted-proxy or Pinchy-style front layers as the supported team-deployment path.

recommendation.title: Design Unified Principals
recommendation.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal contract that covers per-user tokens, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation/revocation, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: nickytonline introduced the current identity-bearing trusted-proxy auth path, making them the best available owner signal for the Gateway user-auth boundary choice.
